_why:
Steps held longer in the deck than they ran in the recording, as a factor on every frame. Only for a slide that is text on a screen. Anything with a pod, a queue or a node in it stays at the speed it really ran -- stretching a cluster would be a lie, stretching words appearing on a card is not.

Keyed by slide, falling back to the step: `1.2.3` uses its own entry if it has one and `1.2`'s otherwise, because holding is normally a property of the step. Step 0 is the only entry. It is the title card and the seven introductions, about two hundred words, typed onto the screen in the thirty-two seconds the run took, which is twice as fast as a room reads. Both of its slides want the same factor, so it is written once against the step and the fallback finds it.

Read by both film.mjs, which does the stretching, and extract.py, which tells the notes how long the slide is.
